card.title: FINNISH BOYS
card.flavorText: Infantry Regiment 200, also known as the "Finnish Boys" (Soomepoisid), was a Finnish Army unit mainly made up of Estonian volunteers. Formed in early 1944 during the Continuation War under Field Marshal Mannerheim’s command, the regiment fought in the defensive battles on the Karelian Isthmus and near the Bay of Viipuri as part of the Finnish 10th Division. After Finland signed an armistice with the Soviet Union in September 1944, the Estonian volunteers faced a difficult situation. Many returned to Estonia, where they were often persecuted by the Soviet regime, while others fled to Sweden or joined other military units. Many fought against the Red Army with the 20th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS, despite initially escaping to Finland to avoid such service. The Finnish Boys' story reflects the challenges faced by Estonians caught between Soviet and German forces during WWII.
